functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

functions.name: sqf
functions.body: block([k:1,i:2],while i*i<=n do (if mod(n,i*i)=0 then (n:n/(i*i),k:k*i) else i:i+1),[k,n])

questiontext:
Solve the following quadratic equation by using the quadratic formula:

\[ {{CT:0}} = 0. \]

Give your answer as a set \(\left(\mbox {e.g.} \ \left\{x_1 , x_2\right\} \right)\):

\({{CT:1}} \in \) [[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]

How to enter: a square root as sqrt(...), e.g. sqrt(5*x). Other roots as a power, with brackets around the exponent: \(\sqrt[3]{x+1}\) is entered as (x+1)^(1/3).
generalfeedback:
Outline: Identify the coefficients \(a,b,c\), compute the discriminant \(\Delta=b^2-4ac\), and substitute into the quadratic formula; then simplify the two roots.
Step 1 — The coefficients
The equation has the form \(a{{CT:1}}^2+b{{CT:1}}+c=0\) with

\[ a={{CT:2}},\qquad b={{CT:3}},\qquad c={{CT:4}} \]

The quadratic formula is

\[ {{CT:1}}_{1,2}=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} \]

Step 2 — The discriminant
First we compute the expression under the square root:

\[ \Delta=b^2-4ac=[[if test="{{CT:21}}"]]{{CT:3}}[[else]]\left({{CT:3}}\right)[[/if]]^2-4\cdot [[if test="{{CT:22}}"]]{{CT:2}}[[else]]\left({{CT:2}}\right)[[/if]]\cdot [[if test="{{CT:23}}"]]{{CT:4}}[[else]]\left({{CT:4}}\right)[[/if]][[if test="{{CT:24}}"]]={{CT:5}}-{{CT:6}}[[else]]={{CT:5}}+{{CT:7}}[[/if]]={{CT:8}} \]

\(\Delta>0\), so the equation has two different real roots. Its square root:[[if test="{{CT:25}}"]]

\[ \sqrt{\Delta}=\sqrt{{{CT:8}}} \]

[[else]]

\[ \sqrt{\Delta}=\sqrt{{{CT:8}}}=[[if test="{{CT:26}}"]]{{CT:9}}[[else]][[if test="{{CT:25}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:11}}[[/if]][[/if]] \]

[[/if]]
Step 3 — Substituting into the formula

\[ {{CT:1}}_{1,2}=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}=\frac{{{CT:12}}\pm [[if test="{{CT:26}}"]]{{CT:9}}[[else]][[if test="{{CT:25}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:11}}[[/if]][[/if]]}{{{CT:13}}} \]

[[if test="{{CT:26}}"]]\(\Delta\) is a perfect square, so both roots are rational. Taking the \(+\) sign and the \(-\) sign separately:

\[ {{CT:1}}_1=\frac{{{CT:12}}+{{CT:9}}}{{{CT:13}}}={{CT:14}},\qquad {{CT:1}}_2=\frac{{{CT:12}}-{{CT:9}}}{{{CT:13}}}={{CT:15}} \]

The solution set is

\[ {{CT:1}}\in {{CT:16}} \]

[[else]][[if test="{{CT:27}}"]]Dividing the numerator and the denominator by \({{CT:17}}\):

\[ {{CT:1}}_{1,2}=[[if test="{{CT:28}}"]]{{CT:18}}\pm [[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]][[else]]\frac{{{CT:18}}\pm [[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]]}{{{CT:20}}}[[/if]] \]

[[/if]]So the two roots are

\[ {{CT:1}}_1=[[if test="{{CT:28}}"]]{{CT:18}}+[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]][[else]]\frac{{{CT:18}}+[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]]}{{{CT:20}}}[[/if]],\qquad {{CT:1}}_2=[[if test="{{CT:28}}"]]{{CT:18}}-[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]][[else]]\frac{{{CT:18}}-[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]]}{{{CT:20}}}[[/if]] \]

The solution set is

\[ {{CT:1}}\in \left\{[[if test="{{CT:28}}"]]{{CT:18}}+[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]][[else]]\frac{{{CT:18}}+[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]]}{{{CT:20}}}[[/if]],\ [[if test="{{CT:28}}"]]{{CT:18}}-[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]][[else]]\frac{{{CT:18}}-[[if test="{{CT:29}}"]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[else]]{{CT:19}}[[/if]]}{{{CT:20}}}[[/if]]\right\} \]

[[/if]]
